posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked: There are some people who just don't care for the way Sentinels plays.  It can be frustratingly random at times; deep strategy players won't care for the way things can turn out, and may feel that the game (or at least some heroes) won't give them enough choices.  This is totally valid.  My last non-solo game featured not one but two players who, while they thought the game was okay, weren't big fans of it.  One spent the entire game bemusedly saying he couldn't get anything to work right and we were all going to die (which it turns out we did, though it was not inevitable, just a spot of bad luck).  The other one played a character picked more or less at random, appeared more than a little bored, and was less than amused when he got abruptly killed by The Grave Beckons just as he and the other survivor were stabilizing.  It's an excellent game for certain sets of values; not all players will share those.  I value the immense variety and replayability, but someone whose favorite game is, say, Chess probably won't go for SOTM.

Yup, the 6th of April is our next due date for meeting up. It'll be cool to meet some more forum members if any of you do turn up :).

Like Silverleaf, Sentinels is a game that technically I shouldn't like as much as I do - I'm not particularly interested in superheroes and have never read a graphic novel (except The Hobbit). I'm okay with card games (though not the collectible kind like Magic) but really like co-operative games, the latter reason probably being the main one I like Sentinels so much. I much prefer to team up with my fellow players against the AI (well, okay it's not really an AI in Sentinels as it is just an automated deck, really, but you know what I mean ;)) than to play against other players. Even worse if it's a game that can have any element of "ganging up" to defeat a player/team. Not fun, to me. Probably why I didn't really find Sentinels Tactics hugely fun. It was okay, just not really my sort of game. Looking forward to GSF though, even though I never read the rules summary (can never really understand that kind of thing unless I'm actually playing through at the same time, otherwise it's all just a bunch of words) and just know that it's "co-operative play...IN SPACE!" :D.
